title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
description:
# Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

Design a data structure that supports adding lowercase words and searching whether a pattern matches any previously added complete word.

Implement the `WordDictionary` class:

*   `WordDictionary()` initializes the object.
*   `void addWord(String word)` adds `word` so it can be matched later.
*   `boolean search(String word)` returns `true` if at least one added word has the same length as `word` and matches every position. A dot `'.'` in the search pattern matches exactly one lowercase English letter; any normal letter must match itself.

A prefix of an added word is not a match unless that prefix was also added as a complete word.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example:

**Input**
["WordDictionary", "addWord", "addWord", "addWord", "search", "search", "search", "search"]
[[], ["bad"], ["dad"], ["mad"], ["pad"], ["bad"], [".ad"], ["b.."]]

**Output**
[null, null, null, null, false, true, true, true]

**Explanation**
WordDictionary wordDictionary = new WordDictionary();
wordDictionary.addWord("bad");
wordDictionary.addWord("dad");
wordDictionary.addWord("mad");
wordDictionary.search("pad"); // returns false because no added word is "pad".
wordDictionary.search("bad"); // returns true because "bad" was added.
wordDictionary.search(".ad"); // returns true because the dot can match 'b', 'd', or 'm'.
wordDictionary.search("b.."); // returns true because "bad" matches the pattern.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= word.length <= 25`
*   `word` in `addWord` consists of lowercase English letters.
*   `word` in `search` consists of lowercase English letters or dots `'.'`.
*   Each `search` pattern contains at most `2` dots.
*   At most `10^4` calls will be made to `addWord` and `search`.

examples.output: [null, null, null, null, false, true, true, true]

tests.description: Canonical workflow covering an absent exact word, an exact match, a leading wildcard, and a trailing multi-character wildcard pattern.
Searching before any add must fail; a dot matches one letter, not zero or two letters.
Different word lengths verify that wildcard matching is exact-length.
A prefix of an added word is not a complete-word match unless that prefix was added separately.
Duplicate insertions must not break exact or wildcard search.
Dots at the beginning, middle, and end should branch only for their own position.
Multiple first-letter branches are matched, while a branch with no stored word must fail.
Two-dot and mixed literal patterns match only words of the same length.
Long words with two dots verify that literal positions still have to line up.
A stored longer word does not imply its prefix, but mixed literal and wildcard positions can still match the complete word.
Words of length one through three make exact-length wildcard behavior visible.
Shared prefixes and separate branches verify that wildcards do not ignore required literal letters.

solutions.name: Trie with Array Children and DFS
solutions.timeComplexity: O(L) addWord, O(26^D * L) worst-case search
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(T) where T is the number of trie nodes
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert every word into a trie whose children are a fixed array of 26 lowercase letters. During search, a normal character follows one child, while a dot recursively tries every non-null child at that depth.

## Key Insight

The trie shares common prefixes, and the recursion only branches when the query actually contains a dot. The terminal marker is checked only after consuming the whole pattern, so prefixes are not accepted as complete words.

## Complexity Analysis
- addWord Time Complexity: O(L)
- search Time Complexity: O(26^D * L) in the worst case, where D is the number of dots
- Space Complexity: O(T)

solutions.name: Trie with HashMap Children and DFS
solutions.timeComplexity: O(L) addWord, O(B^D * L) worst-case search
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(T) where T is the number of stored trie edges
solutions.description:
## Approach

Represent each trie node with a `HashMap<Character, TrieNode>` instead of a 26-slot array. Insert creates missing child nodes with `computeIfAbsent`; search handles a dot by recursively exploring the map values.

## Key Insight

A map-based trie stores only edges that exist, which is often smaller when the alphabet is sparse. The wildcard logic is the same as the array trie, but branching is limited to real children rather than scanning all 26 slots.

## Complexity Analysis
- addWord Time Complexity: O(L)
- search Time Complexity: O(B^D * L) in the worst case, where B is the observed branching factor
- Space Complexity: O(T)

solutions.name: Length Buckets with Direct Pattern Scan
solutions.timeComplexity: O(1) addWord average, O(C * L) search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store words in lists grouped by length. A search pattern only needs to compare against words of the same length; for each candidate, every literal character must match and every dot can match any one character.

## Key Insight

Length bucketing enforces the most important rule before doing character work: the pattern must match a complete word of the same length. This is slower than a trie but is simple and useful as a correctness baseline.

## Complexity Analysis
- addWord Time Complexity: O(1) average after reading the word
- search Time Complexity: O(C * L), where C is the number of stored words with the query length
- Space Complexity: O(N * L)

solutions.name: Wildcard Pattern Index for Up to Two Dots
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the constraint that each search pattern has at most two dots. For every added word, store the exact word, every version with one position replaced by `.`, and every version with two positions replaced by `.`. Then a search is just a set lookup of the query pattern.

## Key Insight

This shifts work from search time to insertion time. Because the problem limits dots to at most two, the number of generated patterns per word is quadratic in word length, which is acceptable for length 25 and gives very fast queries.

## Complexity Analysis
- addWord Time Complexity: O(L^2)
- search Time Complexity: O(L) to hash the pattern
- Space Complexity: O(N * L^2)
